questions.text:
Consider two strings A="qpqrr" and B="pqprqrp". Let x be the length of the longest
common subsequence (not necessarily contiguous) between A and B and let y be the number
of such longest common subsequences between A and B. Then x + 10y = ___.
questions.solution:
A = qpqrr, B = pqprqrp.

The LCS length is x = 4, and the LCSs are: qpqr, qprr, pqrr [latex]\rightarrow[/latex] y = 3.

x + 10y = 4 + 30 = 34

Answer: 34

questions.text:
Consider the tree arcs of a BFS traversal from a source node W in an unweighted, connected,
undirected graph. The tree T formed by the tree arcs is a data structure for computing
questions.solution:
In an unweighted graph BFS visits vertices level by level from W, so the tree path from W to any vertex v has the minimum number of edges.

It does not give shortest paths between other pairs of vertices.

Answer: the shortest path from W to every vertex in the graph

Click here for detail solution by gateoverflow
options: the shortest path between every pair of vertices
the shortest path from W to every vertex in the graph.
the shortest paths from W to only those nodes that are leaves of T.
the longest path in the graph.

questions.text:
Which one of the following correctly determines the solution of the recurrence relation with T(1) = 1?
[latex]T(n)=2T(\frac{n}{2})+logn[/latex]
questions.solution:
Master theorem: a = 2, b = 2, [latex]n^{\log_2 2}=n[/latex].

[latex]f(n)=\log n=O(n^{1-\epsilon})[/latex], so case 1 applies: [latex]T(n)=\Theta(n)[/latex].

Answer: [latex]\Theta(n)[/latex]

questions.text:
The minimum number of comparisons required to find the minimum and the maximum of
100 numbers is _________________.
questions.solution:
Compare elements in pairs (50 comparisons), then find the max among the 50 larger ones (49) and the min among the 50 smaller ones (49).

Total = [latex]\frac{3n}{2}-2=150-2=148[/latex]

Answer: 148

questions.text: Suppose a polynomial time algorithm is discovered that correctly computes the largest clique in a given graph. In this scenario, which one of the following represents the correct Venn diagram of the complexity classes P, NP and NP Complete (NPC)?
questions.solution:
Max-clique is NP-hard, so a polynomial algorithm for it would give P = NP. Then every non-trivial problem in NP is NP-complete, so the classes coincide: P = NP = NPC.

Answer: D
